summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. ErrorScreen takes no error prop and renders only constant text via JSX (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML), so error/stack content can never reach the DOM. Errors are logged only to the local console with console.error; the app has no secrets or PII in game state and nothing is sent over the network. Fault injection lives solely in e2e/support/fault-injection.ts, is installed via Playwright addInitScript/page.evaluate, and nothing under src/ imports it or reads window.__tlhFault/__tlhWorkers, so it cannot ship in dist or be armed by page content. Worker replacement is on-demand only (sharedAdviceClient called on Return Home, bot turns, hint requests); a failed client terminates its worker and removes listeners before being replaced, and a bot failure routes to the error screen which unmounts the table, so an instantly-failing worker yields at most one new worker per user action, not an automatic loop. No new dependencies.
